Transus EDI binnen de Katapull Groep
DeliveryMatch on the Shopify App Store
Katapull breidt Commerce Hub uit met overname van Picqer
Katapull buys WMS provider Picqer to fill out its Commerce Hub
Sendy is nu onderdeel van Sendcloud

items.title: Integration breadth is DeliveryMatch's core asset
items.summary: DeliveryMatch states 200+ connected carriers, 4,000+ users, 40+ connected webshop systems, 75+ ERP/WMS/planning systems and 350+ standard integrations; its timeline records the 100th carrier in 2016 and the 200th integrated system in 2021. The Katapull brand page says 180+ carriers, so carrier counts vary by source and date.
items.implication: Connector coverage and maintenance cost decide competitiveness; carrier counts should be quoted with their source.

items.title: Push-to-pull: the delivery promise starts at the first click
items.summary: Founder Dr. Roland Slegers built DeliveryMatch (founded 2013) on research into e-commerce delivery; its mission framing is 'the last mile starts with the first click'. The dynamic checkout calculates options from stock location, capacity, product data and carrier agreements, and the stock-availability page cites research that 92% of consumers will wait 2 to 7 days if the delivery moment is clear (vendor-cited, original study not named).
items.implication: Checkout options must be feasible, not just cheap or fast; reliability of the promise is the KPI to optimise.

items.title: Returns experience drives repeat purchase (vendor-cited research)
items.summary: DeliveryMatch's returns page cites research that 93% of customers do not buy again after a bad return experience and 84% reorder when returns are quick and simple; it offers a returns portal with merchant-managed reason codes, pre-set return methods and rule-based return costs. Inside Katapull, Returnista is the dedicated returns platform and DeliveryMatch handles return transport.
items.implication: Returns belong in the shipping model, but overlap with Returnista must be managed as a group decision.

items.title: Positioned as a control layer, not only a label printer
items.summary: DeliveryMatch contrasts itself with shipping tools that only execute: it adds transport cost calculation (purchase and sales), CO2 per carrier, Carrier Invoice Control (freight audit) and exception management, and calls itself an independent control layer that avoids long IT projects.
items.implication: Cost and performance bricks (rates, freight audit, scorecards, CO2) are differentiators for B2B shippers and 3PLs.

items.title: 3PLs need a shipping layer above the WMS
items.summary: DeliveryMatch says a WMS supports the warehouse but gives little grip on shipping; 3PLs face many carriers per client, deviating agreements and slow onboarding of new clients. It positions itself for fulfilment environments where standard tools fall short and enterprise platforms are too complex.
items.implication: Multi-client tenancy, client-specific rules and fast client onboarding are must-haves for the 3PL segment.

items.title: Software providers get carriers through one integration
items.summary: For software and system providers DeliveryMatch offers 200+ carriers and 50+ fulfilment connections through one integration, standardised API connections and dynamic checkout functions inside the partner's own system; it runs an integration partner programme.
items.implication: The API and partner programme are a distribution channel; partner adoption should be measured, not just integrations built.

items.title: DeliveryMatch is the logistics brand of the Katapull Commerce Hub
items.summary: DeliveryMatch's timeline records joining the Katapull group (dated 1 November 2024 on its site) as a collaboration of six software companies. Katapull now lists eight labels - Highbiza, Vendit, DeliveryMatch, EffectConnect, Logic4, Transus, Returnista and Picqer (acquired October 2026) - and reports 4,500+ customers in 40+ countries and 27,500+ users at group level. DeliveryMatch publishes integration pages for Logic4, Vendit, EffectConnect, Highbiza, Transus, Returnista and Picqer, and shares its Rotterdam address with Vendit.
items.implication: Bridges to sibling products and joint Commerce Hub offers are a strategic growth lever unique to DeliveryMatch.

items.title: Third-party recognition and security certification support evaluation
items.summary: DeliveryMatch reports being voted best shipping software in the Emerce Top 100 five times in a row (2026), winning the Nederlandse Logistiek Prijs 2025 from the Vereniging Logistiek Management for its contribution to supply-chain control, and obtaining ISO 27001 certification in June 2026.
items.implication: Trust signals matter in Evaluation for ERP-led shippers and 3PLs; ISO 27001 controls must be reflected in tenancy and audit bricks.

items.title: Carriers and brokers use DeliveryMatch as their own TMS
items.summary: For carriers and brokers DeliveryMatch offers connection to customers' webshops, WMS, ERP and sales channels, real-time rate and capacity calculation per customer, management of external carriers and customer contracts, freight audit and transparent reporting.
items.implication: A distinct carrier/broker product with per-customer pricing and audit justifies its own persona and product.

items.title: Wholesalers and manufacturers combine B2B, D2C and marketplaces
items.summary: DeliveryMatch describes wholesalers and manufacturers struggling with many carriers without overview, manual labels and bookings, customer-specific agreements, mixes of pallets, parcels and express, and growing marketplace pressure; it adds a logistics layer on top of ERP and WMS rather than replacing them. Its documents include CMR, customs commercial invoices and ADR documents.
items.implication: Freight, documents and agreements-as-rules are core for this segment.

items.title: Competitors are consolidating
items.summary: Sendcloud reports 30,000+ merchants and absorbed Sendy (which announced it would stop and move users to Sendcloud); nShift, formed in 2021 from Unifaun, Consignor, Transsmart, Returnado and Webshipper, reports 20,000+ customers and 1,000+ carrier connections; Wuunder states it acquired Paazl in 2024.
items.implication: DeliveryMatch competes as a smaller, logistics-expert and ecosystem-backed player; differentiation must come from complex scenarios, control features and the Katapull chain rather than carrier count.

items.title: Implementation speed is part of the promise
items.summary: DeliveryMatch states WMS integrations can be implemented within two months and the Katapull page promises fast implementation without long IT projects, with a fixed project manager from demo to go-live.
items.implication: Time to go-live is a measurable retention driver and should be tracked per segment.
